entries.test: Marcus's dated public writings would show whether he had repeatedly called OpenAI the possible WeWork of AI over an extended period before this post.
entries.note: This is a factual claim about his past statements, despite the speculative analogy within them. He is quoting himself.
The central claim proposes possible harm transmitted from OpenAI to its business partners. “May” leaves that causal outcome uncertain.

entries.test: Contemporaneous SpaceX share and bond prices and public investment commentary would establish the stated daily and weekly performance, bond losses, and increasing promotion as an AI investment.
entries.note: The surrounding price figures give “lost steam” and “doing badly” concrete financial meanings.

entries.test: Historical share prices for the six named companies over the month preceding June 26, 2026 would establish whether their declines matched the stated percentages.
entries.note: The monthly horizon naturally carries through to the abbreviated SoftBank statement.
“In shambles” is an evaluative judgment without a shared factual threshold. The accompanying assertion of widespread criticism is separately checkable.

entries.test: Smith's chart, its underlying data, and his accompanying argument would show whether they establish only revenue growth or also increasing profitability, sustainability, and the absence of a bubble.
entries.note: Marcus challenges what the cited evidence establishes; he does not assert here that revenue failed to rise.

entries.test: Public reporting on Anthropic's commercial performance through June 26 versus April and May, customer usage, Chinese competition, and the Fable pause would test whether those developments worsened its business conditions.
entries.note: The profitability discussion supplies a plain commercial reading of “not as kind.” In context, “with” attributes the deterioration to the listed developments.
This is an emphatic framing of the embedded post, without a distinct testable outcome or threshold.
